paragraphs: R’ Yochanan ben Torta. (A Tanna, a colleague of R’ Akiva.)

Hyman cites Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 4:5,21a: when R’ Akiva called Ben Koziva the King Messiah, R’ Yochanan ben Torta told him, “Akiva, grass will grow on your cheeks, and the son of David will still not have come.” Hyman also cites ש״ר at the beginning of chapter 1 for the episode found in Shemot Rabbah 40:1. Yochanan comes before R’ Akiva, who tells him, “Stand and read the Torah.” He replies, “I have not reviewed the portion,” and the Sages praise him. Yoma 9a preserves his explanation that Shiloh was destroyed because of contempt for sacred things and forbidden sexual relations. Hyman cites Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:10 for the saying found at 7:10 in the consulted text: even after a person dies, his lips move in the grave.

notes.text: The work abbreviated ש״ר in the Torah-reading story remains unidentified here. The Taanit suffix 21a is a folio, not the end of a halakhah range. The heading’s provisional origin remains in the underlying record.

No new primary scalar was returned. The earlier finite ShemotRabbah1 nonmatch and later phrase-search miss leave ש״ר unidentified; they do not prove global absence or another work. The imperative is STAND AND READ, the reply is I HAVE NOT REVIEWED, and BEGINNING chapter1 is retained. Taanit21a is an edition folio beside4:5, not a range. Provisional heading/boundary provenance remains. Akiva’s personal name is locally spelled out, but that is not evidence for expanding his title. All uninspected abbreviated titles stay R-prime; the NOT-YET-coming negation, Shiloh’s two causes and lips-in-grave saying remain.

The Torah-reading exchange is in Shemot Rabbah 40:1. Akiva addresses Yochanan, who answers the people present that he has not reviewed the portion. Hyman’s print (vol. II, p. 686) gives ש״ר רפ״א, even though the consulted passage is at the beginning of chapter 40. The consulted Shir HaShirim Rabbah 7:10 has the lips-in-the-grave saying under Yochanan ben Tortah (תורתה), beside Hyman’s 4:10 citation. The checked Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 4:5 prints the explicit negation in brackets. Yoma states the two causes of Shiloh’s destruction at the end of 9a and explains them over the page turn. Hyman’s separate entry about a cow is a separate notice here.
